Preface During the development of the original Hydropower Supply Chain Gap Analysis report,1 the long lead times associated with large power transformers emerged as a key concern for the hydropower industry, prompting further examination. Procurement constraints for this critical component stem from broader issues, including limited global manufacturing capacity and competition for specialized components and upstream raw materials. These factors highlight the need for a clearer understanding of the supply conditions affecting transformer availability and their potential implications for hydropower project planning. The Hydropower Supply Chain Gap Analysis report, published in August 2024, was developed in response to Executive Order 14017, which directed federal agencies to evaluate the resilience of critical U.S. supply chains. The report was prepared by the U.S. Department of Energy’s Office of Energy Efficiency and Renewable Energy to assess domestic manufacturing capacity for critical hydropower components and identify supply chain gaps. The primary objective of the report was to provide a targeted evaluation of the domestic hydropower supply chain, with an emphasis on identifying key constraints and informing strategies to strengthen U.S. manufacturing capabilities. A specific focus was given to large hydropower systems (>100 MW), where supply chain issues are most pronounced and have significant implications for project development timelines and broader energy system objectives. This supplemental report provides a more detailed analysis of those upstream materials and manufactured product supply chains. By outlining the structural factors that contribute to procurement delays, this report aims to offer information that supports more effective forecasting and early decision-making. The intent is to help hydropower stakeholders anticipate challenges and consider planning measures that may reduce the impact of large power transformer procurement constraints. 1 Putsche, Vicky, Tessa Greco, Elise DeGeorge, and Michael Ingram. 2024.
